features.name: Progressive Profiling
features.summary: Collect profile attributes across the first several sessions instead of requesting everything on the first screen.

features.name: Bulk Timesheet Approval
features.summary: Let an administrator approve many submitted timesheets in a single action.

features.name: Streak Rescue
features.summary: Detect a streak that is about to break and offer the user a way to keep it.

requirements.title: Progressive Profiling for New Tenants
requirements.summary: Reduce time-to-value for new tenants by deferring non-essential profile questions out of the first session.

requirements.title: Progressive Profiling for New Tenants
requirements.summary: Reduce time-to-value for new tenants by deferring non-essential profile questions out of the first session, and capture partial progress so it is not lost when a user abandons a session.

requirements.title: Streak Recovery Policy
requirements.summary: A user who has already lost a streak may restore it once per calendar month at no cost.

pbis.title: Ask for tax details during the first session
pbis.description: Currently we ask for tax details before anyone has seen any value, and people bounce. Move the question later in the ramp.
colloquial_terms: asking for tax details up front

pbis.title: Save partial profile when a user abandons the session
pbis.description: If someone leaves halfway through the ramp we throw their answers away. Keep them and pick up where they left off.

pbis.title: Approve 20 or more timesheets in one action
pbis.description: Managers are approving timesheets one at a time. Needs a bulk action.

pbis.title: Offer a freeze before a streak breaks
pbis.description: Show an option to hold the streak when it is about to lapse.

pbis.title: Let people restore a streak they already lost
pbis.description: One free restore per month, per the written policy.

components.name: Identity Service
components.notes: Handles authentication and session issuance for all tenants.

components.name: Tenant Config Store
components.notes: Stores per-tenant configuration, including which profile questions are pending.

components.name: Push Relay
components.notes: Third-party push notification relay. Delivery is not guaranteed by our SLA.

tickets.reported_symptom: New signups get asked for tax details straight away and a lot of them never come back.
People are upset that they cannot get a streak back after it already broke. They did not know there was a freeze.

decisions.decision: We will not ask for optional profile attributes in the first session.
decisions.rationale: Analytics from the first quarter showed abandonment concentrated on the first-run setup screen, and optional attributes were the largest contributor.

decisions.decision: A freeze is offered proactively, not only after the streak has broken.
decisions.rationale: Post-hoc restore reads as a penalty. Offering it in advance does not.

topics: losing answers when someone drops out of the ramp is the top complaint
decided to persist partial profile rather than re-ask
still open: how long do we keep a partial profile before discarding it
two tickets look like the same thing, need to check before we build twice
push relay is flaky, cannot rely on it for time-critical messages

runbooks.title: Push Relay delivery failure runbook
steps: Check relay status page for an active incident.
Confirm the tenant's device token is still valid in the config store.
If the relay is degraded, fall back to in-app messaging.
Record the incident window for the weekly reliability review.

dependencies.description: Progressive Profiling depends on the Identity Service for session-scoped tenant context.
PBI-A-011 depends on the Tenant Config Store, because deferring the tax question requires persisting which questions are still pending per tenant.
REQ-A-02 depends on the Identity Service for per-session tenant context.
Bulk Timesheet Approval depends on Progressive Profiling, because the approval screen shows profile completeness and cannot be built before the ramp exists.
PBI-B-021 depends on the Push Relay, which is a third party and outside the product team's control.
PBI-B-022 and PBI-B-021 substantially duplicate each other. Both concern recovering a broken streak, and they may be the same work.
PBI-B-022 depends on the Event Bus to publish a streak-restored event.

conflicts.description: REQ-A-01 v1.0 and REQ-A-02 v2.0 describe the same feature with different scope. v1.0 omits partial-progress capture.
REQ-B-01 states a one-free-restore-per-month policy. PBI-B-022 describes restoration without stating the monthly limit, and PBI-B-021 describes a freeze that the policy does not mention.
